verdict.rationale: Railway's cloud agents keep running on a remote machine after you disconnect, and the built-in Railway Agent can act on your behalf (configuring services, diagnosing failures, opening PRs). That gives some background, autonomous agent execution. However, the Railway Agent is chat-initiated, and nothing shows user-defined automations that trigger or recur on their own; the condition-based alerts are notifications, not automations. missing for 10: scheduled/recurring automations (cron-style), event-triggered autonomous workflows, documentation of setting up unattended automations, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Your files stay on the agent's disk, and the machine stays running when you disconnect.
It can operate the platform on your behalf: creating and configuring services, inspecting deployments, diagnosing failures, and opening pull requests to fix broken builds.
Claude Code runs on the remote machine, with its development tools and persistent disk
